step_title: Enable Industry Cloud License and Core Permissions
description: Activate the industry cloud license feature, assign the core permission set group to administrators, and verify the admin console is accessible. This is the prerequisite for all other module activation.
prerequisites: Industry Cloud license provisioned by account team
configuration_details: Navigate to Setup > Feature Settings > Industries and enable the life sciences feature toggle
Assign the core admin permission set group to at least one system administrator
Verify the Admin Console app appears in the App Launcher
Confirm the core standard objects (Account, Contact, Product) have the industry-specific fields visible
validation_steps: Open the Admin Console — confirm it loads without errors
Check that industry-specific record types are available on Account and Contact
Verify the industry-specific page layouts are deployed
Run a basic SOQL query on the core objects to confirm field-level security is correct
common_mistakes: Forgetting to assign the permission set group — the admin console will show a blank page without proper permissions
Enabling the feature in production before testing in sandbox — always test in sandbox first
Confusing the industry cloud permission set with the standard platform permission set — they are separate
Not verifying that the managed package version matches the org's API version

description: Set up the territory model with hierarchy levels (nation > region > district > territory), assign accounts to territories, and link users to their territory assignments.
prerequisites: Enterprise Territory Management feature enabled in org
configuration_details: Enable Enterprise Territory Management in Setup > Territory Settings
Create a Territory Model — define the hierarchy levels matching your organization structure
Define territory types (e.g., Sales, Medical, Key Account) as separate branches if needed
Create territory records at each level and establish parent-child relationships
Assign accounts to territories using rules (geography-based) or manual assignment
Assign users to territories with appropriate roles (owner, member, viewer)
validation_steps: Navigate to the Territory Model and verify the hierarchy renders correctly
Check a sample account — confirm it shows the correct territory assignment
Check a sample user — confirm they can see accounts in their assigned territory
Run the territory assignment rules and verify the expected account-to-territory mapping
Verify that sharing rules derived from territory assignments are working (user can view/edit accounts in their territory)
common_mistakes: Building territory hierarchy before cleaning account data — duplicates and incorrect addresses cause misalignment
Not activating the territory model after building it — assignments won't take effect until the model is activated
Using a single territory model for both commercial and medical teams — consider separate models if compliance requires separation
Forgetting to set up forecast integration if territory-based forecasting is needed

step_title: Configure Visit Records, Call Types, and Call Objectives
description: Set up the Visit object with call types, visit statuses, call objectives, and the mobile-optimized page layouts that field reps use during customer visits.
configuration_details: Configure the Visit object record types for different call types (face-to-face, phone, virtual, group)
Set up visit status picklist values (Planned, In Progress, Completed, Cancelled)
Create call objective templates linked to therapeutic areas and product lines
Configure the visit page layout for mobile — prioritize key fields and related lists
Set up visit-related objects: Discussion Topics, Attendees, Visit Products
Configure auto-population rules (e.g., pre-populate products from the account's formulary)
Enable geolocation check-in if GPS-based visit verification is required
validation_steps: Create a test visit on mobile — verify all required fields and related lists are visible
Complete a test visit workflow: plan > check-in > add discussion topics > complete
Verify that completed visits appear in the correct reports and dashboards
Test offline visit creation and sync — create a visit offline and verify it syncs correctly
Confirm visit history is visible on the Account and Contact detail pages
common_mistakes: Overloading the visit page layout with too many fields — mobile performance degrades with more than 20-25 fields on a page
Not configuring offline sync scope to include visit-related objects — reps lose access to discussion topics and attendees offline
Forgetting to set up sharing rules for visit records — managers may not see their team's visits
Using custom Lightning components on the visit page without testing on the mobile app — not all components render correctly on mobile

step_title: Configure Sample Products, Lots, Allocations, and Signature Capture
description: Set up the complete sample management chain: products eligible for sampling, lot tracking, allocation limits per rep per period, signature capture for compliance, and inventory reconciliation.
prerequisites: Product catalog loaded with sample-eligible products
configuration_details: Mark products as sample-eligible in the product catalog
Create sample lot records with lot numbers, expiration dates, and initial quantities
Configure allocation rules: set maximum quantities per rep per product per time period
Set up sample transaction types (Drop, Transfer, Return, Adjustment, Receipt)
Configure signature capture settings: require signature for drops, set signature format (wet-ink or electronic)
Set up sample inventory reconciliation schedule (typically monthly)
Configure validation rules to enforce PDMA/local regulatory limits
Enable sample limit calculations (batch job or real-time, depending on volume)
validation_steps: Drop a sample on a test visit — verify lot selection, quantity validation, and signature capture work
Exceed the allocation limit — verify the system blocks the transaction with a clear error
Process a sample return — verify inventory adjusts correctly
Run the inventory reconciliation report — verify counts match expected values
Test signature capture on tablet — verify the signature image is stored and linked to the transaction
Verify sample transaction history on the HCP record
common_mistakes: Not setting up lot tracking from the start — retrofitting lots after go-live is extremely painful
Setting allocation limits at the wrong granularity (per quarter vs per month) — changing this later affects all historical data
Forgetting to configure the batch calculation job for sample limits — reps see stale limit data
Not testing signature capture on the actual target device — simulator behavior differs from hardware
Missing the cold chain / temperature-sensitive product configuration — some samples have special handling rules

step_title: Configure Content Delivery, Approved Presentations, and Email Templates
description: Set up the content management system for delivering approved marketing materials, interactive presentations, and email templates to field users.
prerequisites: Content assets created and approved by compliance
configuration_details: Create content document records for each approved presentation or asset
Organize content into categories by therapeutic area, product line, and audience type
Configure content assignment rules — which content is available to which user profiles and territories
Set up the content player for interactive presentations (HTML5-based)
Configure email templates and approved email fragments
Set up content versioning — link new versions to parent documents, retire outdated versions
Configure content analytics tracking (session-level engagement metrics)
validation_steps: Open a presentation on tablet — verify rendering quality and navigation
Test content availability filters — verify a rep sees only content assigned to their territory/profile
Send a test approved email — verify template renders correctly with merge fields
Test content access offline — verify presentations are available when disconnected
Check content analytics — verify that viewing sessions are recorded with duration and slide data
common_mistakes: Uploading content in the wrong format — the mobile player supports HTML5 and PDF, but not all interactive elements translate
Not testing content offline — large presentations may exceed the mobile sync size limit
Forgetting to retire old content versions — reps continue using outdated materials
Skipping the compliance approval workflow — unreviewed content reaching the field is a regulatory risk
Not configuring content categories before uploading — restructuring categories after content is assigned is disruptive

step_title: Configure Communication Consent, Opt-In/Opt-Out, and Channel Preferences
description: Set up the consent management framework to capture, store, and enforce HCP communication preferences across all engagement channels (email, phone, visit, digital).
prerequisites: Understanding of applicable regulations (GDPR, PDMA, local pharma codes)
configuration_details: Define consent types for each communication channel (email, phone, SMS, face-to-face, digital)
Configure consent purposes (marketing, scientific, sample-related, event invitation)
Set up consent capture forms for mobile and web
Configure consent enforcement rules — block communication attempts to HCPs who have opted out
Set up consent audit trail — every consent change must be tracked with timestamp, source, and old/new values
Configure country-specific consent rules (e.g., GDPR double opt-in for EU, PDMA for US, APPI for Japan)
Define consent expiration policies if applicable (some jurisdictions require periodic re-consent)
validation_steps: Capture consent on a test contact — verify the consent record is created with correct attributes
Opt out a test contact from email — verify that approved email sends are blocked for that contact
Verify the audit trail — check that consent changes are logged with full history
Test the consent capture form on mobile — verify it works offline and syncs correctly
Verify country-specific rules — test that EU contacts require double opt-in while US contacts do not
Confirm there is no global unsubscribe-all capability (platform does not support this by design for compliance reasons)
common_mistakes: Assuming a single consent model works globally — consent rules vary dramatically by country and region
Not capturing consent source and timestamp — required for regulatory audit in most jurisdictions
Confusing consent types and consent purposes — a contact may consent to email for marketing but not for scientific communications
Building a custom unsubscribe-all feature — the platform intentionally does not have this to prevent accidental bulk opt-out
Not testing consent enforcement end-to-end — capturing consent is useless if the enforcement rules are not configured

step_title: Configure Activity Plan Templates, Cycle Frequencies, and Targeting
description: Set up structured visit plans that define how often reps should visit each account based on segmentation, priority, and business rules.
configuration_details: Define activity plan templates for each business unit or therapeutic area
Configure cycle plan periods (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual)
Set target call frequencies by account segment (e.g., A-tier accounts: 4 visits/quarter, B-tier: 2 visits/quarter)
Configure activity plan categories for different activity types (visit, phone, email, event)
Set up activity plan criteria to filter which accounts are included in each plan
Link activity plans to products for product-specific call objectives
Configure reach and frequency thresholds for compliance monitoring
validation_steps: Generate an activity plan for a test territory — verify account inclusion and target frequencies
Verify that completed visits decrement the remaining call count for the period
Check the activity plan dashboard — verify reach and frequency metrics are calculating correctly
Test plan rollover — verify that plans for a new cycle period generate correctly from templates
Confirm that account segment changes (e.g., B-tier to A-tier) update the target frequency
common_mistakes: Setting unrealistic call frequencies — if a rep physically cannot complete the planned calls in a cycle, compliance metrics become meaningless
Not linking activity plans to territory assignments — plans must reflect the rep's actual account list
Confusing activity plan categories with activity plan criteria — categories are the type of activity, criteria are the targeting filters
Not accounting for PTO, training days, and admin time when setting cycle frequency targets
Building overly complex criteria rules — simpler targeting with manual overrides performs better than complex automated rules

step_title: Configure Speaker Programs, Medical Events, and Attendee Tracking
description: Set up event management for speaker programs, advisory boards, medical congresses, and commercial events with attendee tracking, expense management, and compliance controls.
configuration_details: Define event types (speaker program, advisory board, congress, lunch-and-learn, virtual event)
Configure event statuses and approval workflows
Set up attendee management — invite tracking, RSVP, attendance confirmation, no-show handling
Configure speaker management — speaker contracts, fair market value rates, payment tracking
Set up expense tracking categories (venue, catering, travel, speaker fees, materials)
Configure compliance rules — attendee caps per event type, spend limits, cooling-off periods
Enable transparency reporting integration — automatic capture of HCP spend for Sunshine Act / EFPIA
validation_steps: Create a test event — verify all required fields and workflows trigger correctly
Invite a test attendee — verify RSVP tracking and consent check
Record attendance — verify that HCP spend is calculated and linked to the transparency reporting data
Test the approval workflow — verify events require approval before execution
Verify expense tracking — confirm that event costs roll up correctly to the event record
common_mistakes: Not integrating with consent management — inviting HCPs who have opted out of event communications
Forgetting transparency reporting setup — HCP spend from events must flow to Sunshine Act reporting automatically
Under-configuring event types — a single generic event type makes compliance enforcement difficult
Not setting up speaker fair market value validation — paying above FMV is a compliance risk
Missing attendee cap enforcement — regulatory limits on attendees vary by event type and jurisdiction

step_title: Configure Coaching Assessment Forms, Scoring, and Development Plans
description: Set up the field coaching module for managers to evaluate rep performance during ride-alongs using configurable assessment forms with scoring rubrics.
prerequisites: Coaching competency framework defined by sales enablement team
configuration_details: Define coaching assessment templates with competency categories (product knowledge, selling skills, compliance adherence, customer engagement)
Configure scoring rubrics for each competency (1-5 scale with defined criteria for each level)
Set up coaching visit record types — link coaching assessments to visit records
Configure development action plans — template for post-coaching improvement goals
Set up coaching dashboards for manager visibility into team performance trends
Configure coaching report sharing rules — coaching data is sensitive and should follow HR data access patterns
validation_steps: Complete a test coaching assessment during a visit — verify form renders and scores calculate correctly
Verify that coaching scores aggregate at the rep level for trending
Test the development action plan workflow — verify goals are assigned and trackable
Confirm coaching reports are visible only to authorized managers and HR
Test coaching on mobile — verify the assessment form works during offline ride-alongs
common_mistakes: Making coaching forms too long — managers will skip them if they take more than 5-10 minutes to complete
Not separating coaching data access from general CRM access — coaching evaluations are HR-sensitive
Building custom coaching forms instead of using the platform's configurable assessment framework
Forgetting to test coaching offline — most ride-alongs happen in clinical settings with poor connectivity
Not linking coaching outcomes to performance metrics — coaching without measurable impact tracking is just paperwork

step_title: Configure Mobile App Deployment, Sync Scope, and Offline Access
description: Set up the mobile application for field users including data sync configuration, offline access scope, device management, and performance optimization.
prerequisites: All modules requiring mobile access are configured
MDM (Mobile Device Management) solution in place
configuration_details: Configure the mobile sync scope — define which objects, fields, and records sync to the device
Set up sync filters — limit data to the user's territory and relevant time window (e.g., 90 days of history)
Configure offline page layouts — ensure critical pages work without connectivity
Set up push notification configuration for sync status, new assignments, and alerts
Configure mobile security policies (passcode requirements, session timeout, data encryption at rest)
Set up mobile logging for troubleshooting sync issues
Configure mobile app branding (logo, splash screen, color theme)
validation_steps: Install the app on a test device — verify initial sync completes without errors
Test offline mode — enable airplane mode and verify all critical workflows function
Test sync conflict resolution — edit the same record on device and web, then sync
Verify data volume — check that sync scope produces an acceptable data size for the device
Test on multiple device types (iPad, iPhone, Android) to verify cross-platform consistency
Measure initial sync time and incremental sync time — should be under 5 minutes for incremental
common_mistakes: Syncing too much data — including all accounts instead of territory-filtered accounts degrades performance
Not testing on real devices — emulator testing misses performance, connectivity, and rendering issues
Forgetting to configure sync error handling — silent sync failures leave reps with stale data
Setting session timeout too aggressively — reps get locked out during customer meetings
Not planning for initial deployment sync time — first sync for a new rep can take 15-30 minutes with full data
